evidence.quoted_text:
"manager_restarted": (
            (((manager.get("before") or {}).get("manager") or {})
             .get("pid") or 0) > 0
            and (((manager.get("after") or {}).get("manager") or {})
                 .get("pid") or 0) > 0
            and (manager.get("before") or {}).get("manager", {}).get("pid")
            != (manager.get("after") or {}).get("manager", {}).get("pid")
            and bool(((manager.get("before") or {}).get("manager") or {})
                     .get("invocation_id"))
            and bool(((manager.get("after") or {}).get("manager") or {})
                     .get("invocation_id"))
            and (manager.get("before") or {}).get("manager", {}).get("invocation_id")
            != (manager.get("after") or {}).get("manager", {}).get("invocation_id")),
evidence.reason: The current `manager_restarted` check only verifies nonempty, differing manager PIDs and invocation IDs. It never requires the guest `boot_id` to be unchanged across that restart. A guest reboot can change both PID and invocation ID, so it can satisfy `manager_restarted`; because `boot_id_changed` is checked separately, a later reboot can still satisfy the reboot check. This is an existing false-positive in the intended validation behavior, not a new requirement.
